::: {.manual-prereq title="Separate New Deliveries From The Frozen Migration Baseline"}

The new data is **not in the May 2025 ZIP**. Its sources are declared as
`harvard_2025_2026` and the separately staged `july_2025_candidate` item in
`stagecoach_manifest.yml`. Stage those declared items before running the
survey. Resolve project files with `here::here()` and source locations from
the manifest; do not reconstruct the former broad Drive staging path.
The ZIP remains the source of truth for the old-wave migration and its
comparison outputs. New-wave discovery is a separate, explicitly scoped use
of the staged delivery tree; do not reintroduce that tree into page 16's
old-wave inventory.

Stagecoach owns the source locations. The graph inventories the staged CSVs
and tracks each file's contents with `format = "file"`. The inventory is
refreshed on each build to detect added and removed deliveries. Ingestion
records the bytes it read through source hashes; that snapshot is derived
provenance, not a second input registry. Do not modify source files.

Kai's Python work under `sandbox/validation/06_new_w3/` is exploratory evidence,
not an executable dependency. In particular, `crosswalk_new_to_old.py` also
includes the sibling `Raw/RMA 2025 - july` delivery. Its inclusion and maximum reduction were authorized on 2026-11-08. Keep
its identity and coverage visible in the audits. Folder names
are delivery labels, not verified reporting periods.

::: {.manual-procedure title="Declare The Source Inventory Helpers"}

Load these definitions by running their chunks, or from the repository root:

```r
helpers <- knitr::purl(
  here::here("notebooks", "pipeline", "26_page-prep-2025-2026.qmd"),
  output = tempfile(fileext = ".R"), documentation = 0L, quiet = TRUE
)
for (expr in parse(helpers)) {
  if (is.call(expr) && identical(expr[[1L]], as.name("<-")) &&
      is.call(expr[[3L]]) && identical(expr[[3L]][[1L]], as.name("function"))) eval(expr)
}
```

The loader above evaluates function definitions only. Target declarations
are reserved for the graph. User-run examples use plain R fences. The source
resolver follows Stagecoach's `input directory/source/item name/source
basename` layout. It rebases the manifest's project-local input directory
through `here::here()` so host absolute paths do not leak into the container.
The two source patterns are explicit directory paths, not discovery globs.

```{r}
s8_new_wave_roots_fn <- function(manifest_path = here::here("stagecoach_manifest.yml")) {
  manifest <- yaml::read_yaml(manifest_path, eval.expr = FALSE)
  source <- manifest$sources[["01_gold_mine"]]
  if (!isTRUE(source$enabled)) stop("Stagecoach's 01_gold_mine source is disabled.")
  project <- sub("/+$", "", manifest$project$project_working_dir)
  input <- manifest$project$input_data_dir
  if (length(project) != 1L || length(input) != 1L || !startsWith(input, paste0(project, "/"))) {
    stop("The Stagecoach input directory must be inside its declared project directory.")
  }
  input_relative <- substring(input, nchar(project) + 2L)
  ids <- c("harvard_2025_2026", "july_2025_candidate")
  items <- lapply(ids, function(id) {
    hits <- Filter(function(x) identical(x$name, id), source$items)
    if (length(hits) != 1L) stop("Expected one Stagecoach item named ", id)
    pattern <- hits[[1L]]$path_regex
    if (length(pattern) != 1L || !nzchar(pattern) ||
        any(vapply(c("*", "?", "["), function(x) grepl(x, pattern, fixed = TRUE), TRUE))) {
      stop("New-wave Stagecoach items must name explicit source directories: ", id)
    }
    hits[[1L]]
  })
  tibble::tibble(
    source_id = ids,
    root = vapply(items, function(item) {
      here::here(input_relative, "01_gold_mine", item$name, basename(item$path_regex))
    }, ""),
    scope = c("approved Harvard delivery", "approved separate July delivery")
  )
}

s8_new_wave_inventory_fn <- function(roots, hash = FALSE) {
  stopifnot(nrow(roots) > 0L, !anyDuplicated(roots$source_id))
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(roots)), function(i) {
    root <- roots$root[[i]]
    if (!dir.exists(root)) stop("Delivery root is unavailable: ", root)
    relative <- sort(list.files(root, recursive = TRUE, full.names = FALSE,
                                include.dirs = FALSE), method = "radix")
    paths <- file.path(root, relative)
    info <- file.info(paths)
    parts <- strsplit(relative, "/", fixed = TRUE)
    tibble::tibble(
      source_id = roots$source_id[[i]], relative_path = relative, path = paths,
      delivery = vapply(parts, function(x) if (length(x) >= 3L) x[[2L]] else roots$source_id[[i]], ""),
      extension = tolower(tools::file_ext(paths)), bytes = info$size,
      modified = info$mtime,
      content_md5 = if (hash) unname(tools::md5sum(paths)) else rep(NA_character_, length(paths))
    )
  }))
}

s8_new_wave_metadata_fn <- function() {
  c(paste0("orgunitlevel", 1:5), "organisationunitid", "organisationunitname",
    "organisationunitcode", "organisationunitdescription", "periodid",
    "periodname", "periodcode", "perioddescription")
}

s8_new_wave_header_fn <- function(path) {
  columns <- names(readr::read_csv(
    path, n_max = 0L, col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character()),
    name_repair = "minimal", show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE
  ))
  if (anyNA(columns) || any(!nzchar(columns)) || anyDuplicated(columns)) {
    stop("Review empty or repeated source headers before reading: ", path)
  }
  columns
}
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Read Raw Text Through DuckDB"}

Keep all source fields as `VARCHAR` initially. Preserve identifier spelling,
leading zeros, and measurement tokens for the conversion audit on page 27.
Empty fields are null; literal `NA` remains text at this raw boundary. This is
an intentional difference from the already-curated numeric reader on page 18.
No coercion, renaming, grouping, row filtering, or automatic error skipping
occurs here. Header checks fail before DuckDB can silently repair duplicates.

```{r}
s8_new_wave_literal_fn <- function(x) {
  paste0("'", gsub("'", "''", x, fixed = TRUE), "'")
}
s8_new_wave_identifier_fn <- function(x) {
  paste0('"', gsub('"', '""', x, fixed = TRUE), '"')
}
s8_new_wave_csv_sql_fn <- function(path) {
  stopifnot(length(path) == 1L, file.exists(path))
  paste0("read_csv(", s8_new_wave_literal_fn(path),
         ", header=true, delim=',', quote='\"', escape='\"', ",
         "all_varchar=true, nullstr='', strict_mode=true, ignore_errors=false)")
}
s8_new_wave_read_fn <- function(path) {
  original <- s8_new_wave_header_fn(path)
  relation <- duckplyr::read_sql_duckdb(
    paste0("SELECT * FROM ", s8_new_wave_csv_sql_fn(path)), prudence = "stingy"
  )
  if (!identical(names(relation), original)) stop("DuckDB changed the source header: ", path)
  relation
}

s8_new_wave_shape_fn <- function(path) {
  relation <- s8_new_wave_read_fn(path)
  required <- c("organisationunitid", "periodcode", "periodname")
  missing <- setdiff(required, names(relation))
  if (length(missing)) stop("Missing survey keys in ", path, ": ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
  source <- s8_new_wave_csv_sql_fn(path)
  query <- paste0(
    "SELECT count(*) AS rows, count(DISTINCT organisationunitid) FILTER ",
    "(WHERE organisationunitid IS NOT NULL AND trim(organisationunitid) NOT IN ('','NA')) AS clinics, ",
    "count(*) FILTER (WHERE organisationunitid IS NULL OR trim(organisationunitid) IN ('','NA')) AS missing_uid, ",
    "count(*) FILTER (WHERE periodcode IS NULL OR trim(periodcode) IN ('','NA')) AS missing_period, ",
    "count(*) FILTER (WHERE periodcode IS NOT NULL AND trim(periodcode) NOT IN ('','NA') ",
    "AND NOT regexp_full_match(periodcode, '[0-9]{4}(0[1-9]|1[0-2])')) AS invalid_period, ",
    "(SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT organisationunitid,periodcode FROM ", source,
    " GROUP BY organisationunitid,periodcode)) AS clinic_month_keys FROM ", source
  )
  duckplyr::read_sql_duckdb(query, prudence = "stingy") |>
    dplyr::collect() |>
    dplyr::mutate(columns = length(names(relation)),
                  measurement_columns = length(setdiff(names(relation), s8_new_wave_metadata_fn())))
}
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Write The Raw Parquet Boundary"}

The writer is called by one file-target branch. It records a content hash
and checks it again after the read, preserving every source column and
adding provenance fields. Targets tracks each input CSV directly.
The source-row field is a read-time record ordinal, not a physical CSV line
number or a stable clinic identifier. These raw Parquet products retain the
observed source snapshot. They do not replace the staged source CSVs or the
old-wave baseline.

```{r}
s8_new_wave_write_raw_fn <- function(path, output_path, source_id, relative_path, expected_md5 = NULL) {
  if (is.null(expected_md5)) expected_md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(path))
  stopifnot(length(expected_md5) == 1L, !is.na(expected_md5), nzchar(expected_md5),
            length(source_id) == 1L, length(relative_path) == 1L,
            identical(unname(tools::md5sum(path)), expected_md5))
  relation <- s8_new_wave_read_fn(path)
  reserved <- c("_source_file", "_source_row", "_source_id", "_source_md5")
  if (any(reserved %in% names(relation))) stop("Source uses reserved provenance column names.")
  sql <- paste0("SELECT *, ", s8_new_wave_literal_fn(relative_path), " AS _source_file, ",
                "row_number() OVER () AS _source_row, ", s8_new_wave_literal_fn(source_id),
                " AS _source_id, ", s8_new_wave_literal_fn(expected_md5), " AS _source_md5 FROM ",
                s8_new_wave_csv_sql_fn(path))
  dir.create(dirname(output_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  duckplyr::compute_parquet(
    duckplyr::read_sql_duckdb(sql, prudence = "stingy"), output_path
  )
  if (!identical(unname(tools::md5sum(path)), expected_md5)) stop("Source changed during ingestion.")
  output_path
}
```

The execution page branches over the Stagecoach-derived file inventory,
then tracks each CSV and its raw Parquet separately.

:::

The code implements maximum reduction and first nonmissing metadata in stable

::: {.manual-procedure title="Inventory Stagecoach Sources And Describe Each File"}

The execution page refreshes the list of staged CSV paths before each build.
Individual file targets detect content changes. The source snapshot below
records the hashes captured by ingestion as derived provenance; it is never
read back as configuration or as an input-discovery prerequisite.

```{r}
s8_new_wave_sources_fn <- function(roots) {
  x <- s8_new_wave_inventory_fn(roots, hash = FALSE)
  x <- x[x$extension == "csv", c("source_id", "relative_path", "path")]
  if (!nrow(x)) stop("No new-wave CSVs are staged through Stagecoach.")
  if (anyDuplicated(x[c("source_id", "relative_path")])) stop("Repeated staged CSV paths.")
  x$source_file <- paste(x$source_id, x$relative_path, sep = "/")
  x
}
s8_new_wave_snapshot_fn <- function(paths, inventory) {
  hashes <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(paths, function(path) {
    duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(path, prudence = "stingy") |>
      dplyr::distinct(`_source_id`, `_source_file`, `_source_md5`) |>
      dplyr::collect() |>
      dplyr::rename(source_id = `_source_id`, source_file = `_source_file`, content_md5 = `_source_md5`)
  }))
  stopifnot(nrow(hashes) == nrow(inventory), !anyDuplicated(hashes[c("source_id", "source_file")]))
  snapshot <- dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(inventory, source_id, relative_path, source_file), hashes,
    by = c("source_id", "source_file"), relationship = "one-to-one")
  stopifnot(!anyNA(snapshot$content_md5))
  snapshot
}
s8_new_wave_table_key_fn <- function(path) {
  parts <- strsplit(tolower(path), "/", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
  table <- which(grepl("^tableau ", parts))
  key <- paste(parts[seq.int(if (length(table)) tail(table, 1L) else length(parts), length(parts))], collapse = "/")
  key <- gsub("janv\\s*-\\s*juin|juillet\\s*-\\s*dec|\\b[0-9]{6}\\b|\\b20[0-9]{2}\\b", " ", key, perl = TRUE)
  trimws(gsub(" +", " ", gsub(" .csv", ".csv", key, fixed = TRUE)))
}
s8_new_wave_schema_fn <- function(paths) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(paths, function(path) {
    relation <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(path, prudence = "stingy")
    info <- relation |> dplyr::distinct(`_source_id`, `_source_file`) |> dplyr::collect()
    stopifnot(nrow(info) == 1L)
    periods <- relation |> dplyr::distinct(periodcode) |> dplyr::collect()
    cols <- setdiff(names(relation), c("_source_id", "_source_file", "_source_row", "_source_md5"))
    tibble::tibble(source_id = info$`_source_id`, source_file = info$`_source_file`,
      table_key = s8_new_wave_table_key_fn(info$`_source_file`), position = seq_along(cols),
      source_name = cols, is_metadata = cols %in% s8_new_wave_metadata_fn(),
      periods = rep(list(sort(unique(periods$periodcode))), length(cols)))
  }))
}
```

```{r}
s8_new_wave_schema_df <- s8_new_wave_schema_fn(s8_new_wave_raw_parquet)
s8_new_wave_source_snapshot_df <- s8_new_wave_snapshot_fn(s8_new_wave_raw_parquet, s8_new_wave_source_inventory_df)
```

::: {.manual-check title="Survey One File Before Expanding To Every Delivery"}

Run these examples in order from the repository root after loading the helpers.
They read sources and collect small diagnostics; they do not call `tar_make()`
or persist measurement products. Start with one file; the explicit all-file
loops below are for the researcher to run after that first check succeeds.

**1. Inventory the Stagecoach deliveries.** Input discovery and hashing are
part of the R graph; there is no additional preparation script.
Stage the manifest-declared items on the host from the repository root first.
This creates the scoped staging links; it does not execute targets or execute
the approved two-delivery production graph.

```sh
stagecoach stage --manifest stagecoach_manifest.yml
```

```r
roots <- s8_new_wave_roots_fn()
transform(roots, available = dir.exists(root))
# If an item is not yet staged, use the host Stagecoach command below first.
main_inventory <- s8_new_wave_inventory_fn(roots[roots$source_id == "harvard_2025_2026", ])
main_inventory |> dplyr::count(delivery, extension, name = "files")
main_inventory |> dplyr::summarise(files = dplyr::n(), bytes = sum(bytes), .by = extension)
# Inspect TXT/readme/support files in the authorized session as well as CSVs.
main_inventory |> dplyr::filter(extension != "csv")

# Inspect July separately even though it is included in the approved scope.
july_inventory <- s8_new_wave_inventory_fn(roots[roots$source_id == "july_2025_candidate", ])
july_inventory |> dplyr::count(delivery, extension, name = "files")
```

**2. Inspect one header, shape, reporting periods, and a bounded metadata sample.**
The sample may contain clinic identifiers; keep it out of rendered artifacts.

```r
csv_inventory <- main_inventory |> dplyr::filter(extension == "csv")
stopifnot(nrow(csv_inventory) > 0L)
example_path <- csv_inventory$path[[1L]]
raw <- s8_new_wave_read_fn(example_path)
s8_new_wave_shape_fn(example_path)
tibble::tibble(position = seq_along(names(raw)), source_name = names(raw),
               role = ifelse(names(raw) %in% s8_new_wave_metadata_fn(), "metadata", "measurement candidate"))
raw |> dplyr::count(periodcode, periodname, name = "rows") |> dplyr::collect()
raw |> dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(s8_new_wave_metadata_fn())) |> head(5) |> dplyr::collect()
raw |> dplyr::count(organisationunitid, periodcode, name = "rows") |>
  dplyr::filter(rows > 1L) |> head(20) |> dplyr::collect()
# Preserve raw measurement tokens for preliminary content inspection.
measurements <- setdiff(names(raw), s8_new_wave_metadata_fn())
if (length(measurements)) {
  raw |> dplyr::count(.data[[measurements[[1L]]]], sort = TRUE, name = "rows") |>
    head(10) |> dplyr::collect()
}
```

**3. Build file-shape and header inventories across the selected scope.**
These loops scan the selected CSVs. A differing schema may reflect a changed
questionnaire, not a damaged file. Do not union schemas or collapse duplicates
before interpreting the differences.

```r
shapes <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(csv_inventory)), function(i) {
  dplyr::bind_cols(csv_inventory[i, c("source_id", "relative_path", "delivery")],
                   s8_new_wave_shape_fn(csv_inventory$path[[i]]))
})
shapes |> dplyr::summarise(files = dplyr::n(), raw_rows = sum(rows),
                          min_columns = min(columns), max_columns = max(columns), .by = delivery)
headers <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(csv_inventory)), function(i) {
  columns <- s8_new_wave_header_fn(csv_inventory$path[[i]])
  tibble::tibble(source_id = csv_inventory$source_id[[i]],
                 relative_path = csv_inventory$relative_path[[i]], delivery = csv_inventory$delivery[[i]],
                 position = seq_along(columns), source_name = columns,
                 is_metadata = columns %in% s8_new_wave_metadata_fn())
})
headers |> dplyr::filter(!is_metadata) |>
  dplyr::summarise(files = dplyr::n_distinct(relative_path), .by = c(delivery, source_name))
# Check actual period coverage per file, not just delivery-folder labels.
periods <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(csv_inventory)), function(i) {
  s8_new_wave_read_fn(csv_inventory$path[[i]]) |> dplyr::count(periodcode, name = "rows") |>
    dplyr::collect() |> dplyr::mutate(delivery = csv_inventory$delivery[[i]],
                                    relative_path = csv_inventory$relative_path[[i]])
})
periods |> dplyr::count(delivery, periodcode, name = "source_files")
```

**4. Inspect the approved source/reduction policy on page 27.** Which deliveries are distinct
versus revisions? Where does July fill a gap or duplicate another delivery? Which
periods and clinic levels are actually present? Are IDs/periods missing or
malformed? Which headers appear or disappear between deliveries? Are repeated
clinic-month keys within a file expected? Do the encoding, null tokens, and reporting grain agree with the R parameters?

The R pipeline includes both Stagecoach deliveries and maximum reduction.
Retain any exceptions as governed review inputs, rather than copying fixed
assertions from a collaborator's historical counts. Page 27 adds token-conversion
and mapping audits; page 28 checks identity and spatial compatibility.

:::
